source_title: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems

standard_prerequisites.name: Unconfined system
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Steiner triple system is unconfined when it carries an HF-ordering with no maximum.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the inclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Orientation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An orientation of A selects one member of each block as its representative, with the closure condition on the resulting relation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure that has to be produced.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inessential elements
standard_prerequisites.statement: An element belongs to at most one block of A when it is inessential, which makes it convenient to remove in the induction.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the case split of the first induction.

core_obligations: Prove by induction on the cardinality of A that an unconfined system has an orientation, taking an element belonging to at most one block and extending the orientation given by the induction hypothesis (source line 447).
Prove by a second induction on the cardinality of A that every subset X of A of size at most two satisfies the density condition with respect to A (source lines 449-450).

In the second induction, pass from a subset to a larger one and use that the density of the larger set dominates that of the subset, which is at least two by the induction hypothesis (source line 450).

proof_roadmap.step: First induction: extend an orientation by an inessential element.
Second induction: transfer the density bound to larger subsets.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled proposition at source lines 445-446, that the unconfined Steiner triple systems form a subclass of the oriented ones. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 447-451) runs two separate inductions on the cardinality: the first produces an orientation by removing an element that lies in at most one block, the second establishes the density condition for subsets of size at most two by passing to a larger subset and comparing densities. The statement records the inclusion only, and neither the case split of the first induction nor the density comparison of the second appears in it.
